subject: general
question: From a point 30 m away from the base of a tree, the angle of elevation of the top of the tree is 60°. Find the height of the tree (take √3 = 1.73).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the sides opposite to the angles are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The side adjacent to 60° (opposite to 30°) represents the base = 1 part = 30 m.

The side opposite to 60° represents the height of the tree = √3 parts = 30 × √3.

Height = 30 × 1.73 = 51.9 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.9 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 60° A B (Base) C (Top) 30 m h = ? 

**Given:**

Distance of the point from the base of the tree (AB) = 30 m

Angle of elevation of the top of the tree (∠CAB) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

Let the height of the tree (BC) be h.

In right-angled triangle ABC:

⇒ tan(60°) = BC ÷ AB

⇒ √3 = h ÷ 30

⇒ h = 30 × √3

Using the given value √3 = 1.73:

⇒ h = 30 × 1.73

⇒ h = 51.9 m

**∴ The correct answer is 51.9 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when the observer looks upward at an object.

Angle of Depression

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when the observer looks downward at an object. The angle of elevation from an object to an observer is equal to the angle of depression from the observer to the object.

Important Trigonometric Values

tan(30°) = 1 ÷ √3 | tan(45°) = 1 | tan(60°) = √3
